The petitioner is the accused in C.C.No.1274/2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Changanassery.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Changanassery
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The offences against him are under Sections 294(b), 506(i) & 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.

The prosecution case is that ever since the marriage of the petitioner with the de facto complainant on 18.02.2017, she was being subjected to physical and mental cruelty at various places by the accused.

It is alleged that the de facto complainant was subjected to severe tortures during the time when the accused and herself were residing at Mangalapuram, Changanassery, and also at his flat in Sharjah.

There is the allegation raised by the de facto complainant that the accused insisted her to watch and engage in vulgar sexual activities as seen in blue films, and subjected her to severe cruelty whenever she refused to do so.
2. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that there is absolutely no basis for the allegations levelled against him and that the proceedings against him are liable to be quashed.

3. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned counsel 2025:KER:37856 for the second respondent and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.
4.

On going through the final report and the accompanying records relied on by the investigating agency in support of the offences alleged against the accused, it is seen that all the requisite particulars to establish the charge levelled against the accused are brought out.
There are the statements of relevant witnesses to bring out the allegation of physical and mental cruelty meted out to the de facto complainant by the accused.
It is not possible for this Court to sit on judgment on the acceptability of the aforesaid evidence in a proceeding under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
It is up to the Trial Court to analyse the said evidence and arrive at a finding as to whether those evidence are sufficient to warrant a conviction for the offences alleged against the petitioner.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner, by adverting to Annexure-A11, submitted that there had been a compromise between the parties in connection with the case filed by the de facto complainant before the learned Magistrate as C.C.No.112/2022, and hence it is apparent that the allegations levelled against the petitioner is false and 2025:KER:37856 baseless.

I am not inclined to accept the above argument of the learned counsel for the petitioner since it is seen that the aforesaid Justin Sunny Mathew vs State Of Kerala on 30 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/42250232/
2 settlement as evidenced by Annexure-A11, was on 29.09.2022, whereas the allegations against the petitioner pertain to the period starting from 22.02.2017 to 11.04.2023.
6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the second respondent submitted that Annexure-A11 settlement was only in respect of a petition filed by the second respondent before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Changanassery, in connection with the domestic violence coming under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, and that such a settlement was intended only for the purpose of resolving the interim custody of the child.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Changanassery
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: On going through Annexure-A11, it is apparent that the said settlement has been arrived is only for the purpose of making arrangements with regard to the visitorial rights of the petitioner to have interaction with his child.
It is not possible to say that the allegations against the petitioner pertaining to the cruelty meted out to the de facto complainant are false and baseless.
There is absolutely no basis for the contention that the proceedings against the petitioner in C.C.No.1274/2023 are liable to be quashed for the reasons 2025:KER:37856 stated in this petition.
In the result, the petition is hereby dismissed         (Sd/-) G. GIRISH, JUDGE DST/30.05.25 2025:KER:37856
